dicas.texto: Você está no caminho certo! Lembre-se: quando dividimos um inteiro em mais partes iguais, o que acontece com o tamanho de cada fatia individual?
Tente visualizar: se você dividir uma barra de chocolate em 3 pedaços e outra igual em 4, qual pedaço será maior?
Observe as marcas na reta: a marca de 1/3 está mais perto ou mais longe do 1 do que a marca de 1/4?
Compare os pontos marcados: veja qual deles está posicionado mais à direita na reta numérica (mais próximo de 1).
Quando os numeradores são iguais, como o tamanho do denominador afeta o valor da fração?
Olhe para as duas retas: o ponto de Lamara está mais perto do 1 ou mais longe do que o de Orlando?
O ponto que está mais à direita na reta numérica representa o maior valor. Qual deles está mais à direita?
Compare as posições: a marca de 2/3 está depois da marca de 2/4? Se sim, quem comeu mais?

interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Amount Lamara ate" e "Amount Orlando ate"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Lamara ate more of his sandwich."; "Orlando ate more of his sandwich."; "Both ate the same amount of their sandwich."; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir cada reta, marcar cada ponto, escolher a alternativa, concluir).

componentes.papel: campo numérico do denominador da primeira reta (em quantas partes dividir) + confirmar
primeira reta numérica; o aluno marca o ponto da primeira fração
campo numérico do denominador da segunda reta + confirmar
segunda reta numérica; o aluno marca o ponto da segunda fração
seletor com as alternativas de comparação; o aluno escolhe uma delas

passos.acao: In Lamara's number line, divide the interval from 0 to 1 into equal parts and confirm the denominator.
On Lamara's number line, mark the point that represents the fraction she ate.
In Orlando's number line, divide the interval from 0 to 1 into equal parts and confirm the denominator.
On Orlando's number line, mark the point that represents the fraction he ate.
Compare the two marked positions and choose who ate more of the equal-sized sandwich.
passos.valor: Lamara ate more of his sandwich.

passos.acao: After choosing the comparison, click Done to complete the exercise.

erros.devolutiva: The denominator tells how large each piece is. With thirds, each piece is larger than a fourth, so follow the thirds on Lamara's line.
The numerator tells how many parts to count from 0. Do not jump all the way to the denominator mark; count 2 parts of size 1/3.

erros.devolutiva: The halfway point is a useful reference, but two thirds is beyond halfway. Use the second mark on the line divided into thirds.
erros.buggyRule: Tende a colocar qualquer fração próxima de 1/2 como sendo igual a 1/2

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the whole sandwich?
Use the denominator of Lamara's fraction to decide how many equal intervals are needed from 0 to 1.
Look at the bottom number in Lamara's fraction, 2/3, and enter that number.
Enter the number of equal intervals shown by the denominator in 2/3, then confirm the entry.
What does the numerator tell you to count on the number line?
Starting at 0, count equal jumps whose size is one third of the whole.
Make two equal jumps from 0 toward 1.
Click the second division mark after 0 on the line divided into thirds.
What does the denominator describe when a whole sandwich is divided?
Use the bottom number in Orlando's fraction to determine the number of equal intervals.
Read the denominator in Orlando's fraction, 2/4.
Enter the number of equal parts named by the denominator in 2/4, then confirm it.
How many equal parts has Orlando eaten according to the numerator?
Starting at 0, count equal jumps whose size is one fourth of the whole.
Make two equal jumps from 0 toward 1 on the line divided into fourths.
Click the second division mark after 0 on the line divided into four equal parts.
Which marked point is farther to the right on the number line?
Compare how far each fraction is from 0, remembering that both sandwiches are the same size.
Use the halfway point as a reference: 2/4 is halfway, while 2/3 is beyond halfway.
Select the student whose marked point is farther right, then check that the choice says who ate more.
What should you verify before submitting a comparison of fractions less than 1?
Review the two marked positions and the choice shown in the comparison selector.
Make sure the selector contains one of the three provided comparison statements before submitting.
Check the selected comparison, then click the Done button to send the completed exercise.

exercicio.statement:
Lamara and Orlando bought equal-sized fish sandwiches for lunch, and they are enjoying their sandwiches together. Use the number line to find out which student ate more of their sandwich.
Lamara ate 2/3 of his sandwich.
Orlando ate 2/4 of his sandwich.
Who has eaten more of their sandwich?
